solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hunted animals: one may be on board

definitions.meaning: first meaning: wild animals pursued for sport or food
second meaning: chess or draughts is a contest played on a board

explanation.walkthrough: The colon makes it look like one scene of animals on a ship, but each half is a separate meaning of the same short word.
explanation.definitionFit: Quarry such as pheasant or deer is called this, and a pastime played on a board is the same word.

clue.text: Good: a delicate form of illumination

parts.note: slight means delicate, frail or slender

explanation.surface: A soft, gentle kind of lighting is praised as good.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'a delicate' reads as describing the lighting, but it gives A plus SLIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamps burning coal gas were the standard street and household lighting of the Victorian era.

clue.text: Principal Rhine city, not unknown

indicators.note: not means the unknown is left out of the city's name

parts.note: Mainz is a German city on the Rhine
Z is a mathematical unknown, like x and y

explanation.surface: Someone names the chief city on the Rhine but admits it is not well known.
explanation.definitionFit: Main as an adjective means chief or most important, as in the main reason.

clue.text: Tax scheme subsidising Christmas presents?

parts.note: the name of a real UK tax scheme read literally, as if it helped pay for gifts

explanation.walkthrough: The real scheme lets UK charities reclaim basic-rate tax on donations; the clue reads its name literally as help with buying presents.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the British government relief that boosts charitable donations by reclaiming the donor's income tax.

clue.text: Israel's judge sounds a dizzy one

indicators.note: sounds means the name is said to resemble the spoken phrase

parts.note: dizzy means giddy, so a dizzy one is a giddy one

explanation.surface: An Israeli judge is mocked as seeming light-headed.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Old Testament Book of Judges, this leader delivered Israel from the Midianites.

clue.text: What's at beginning of book is often spicier, somehow

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters of often spicier get there by some unstated rearrangement

explanation.surface: A remark that the opening of a book tends to be the racier part.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the illustration facing the title page, found at the very start of a volume.

clue.text: An inner sleeve, we hear, getting straight

indicators.note: we hear means the answer is said like the spoken phrase

parts.note: a lining is an inner sleeve or layer inside a garment

explanation.surface: Someone describes a tailor fitting a sleeve's lining so it hangs straight.
explanation.definitionFit: Bringing things into a straight line or proper position is what this verb describes.

clue.text: Children's author had to come up with line

indicators.note: in a down answer, coming up means the word had is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A children's writer was forced to produce a line of text.
explanation.walkthrough: Roald Dahl wrote Charlie and the Chocolate Factory and Matilda.
explanation.definitionFit: Roald Dahl is among the best-known writers of stories for young readers.

clue.text: Copy needs taking out for checking age

parts.note: a carbon is a carbon copy
taking someone out romantically is dating them

explanation.surface: An editor says a copy of a text needs something removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking out' looks like removal, but it means going on dates.
explanation.definitionFit: Measuring decay of radioactive isotopes lets scientists estimate how old organic remains are.

clue.text: Mixing paint, slipshod in cleaning of equipment

indicators.note: mixing means the letters of paint and slipshod are stirred together into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone stirring paint carelessly while supposedly cleaning gear.
explanation.definitionFit: The military phrase describes meticulous polishing of boots and kit to a high shine.

clue.text: Show displeasure with short volume

indicators.note: short means the word for volume is cut, losing its last letter

parts.note: a volume is a book

explanation.surface: An audience protests at a disappointingly brief book.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeering an act on stage expresses disapproval with this sound.

clue.text: Start in America to gain energy

parts.note: to gain is to get
go means energy or vigour, as in full of go

explanation.surface: Advice to boost your vigour on arriving in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'from the get-go' is US idiom meaning from the very beginning.

clue.text: A batch of loaves? That's odd, maybe unlucky

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a baker's dozen, traditionally one more than twelve
second meaning: an odd number widely thought unlucky

explanation.walkthrough: A baker's dozen is thirteen: bakers added a spare loaf to avoid being accused of selling short.
explanation.definitionFit: The number is a traditional baker's dozen, is odd, and is superstitiously considered ill-omened.

clue.text: More inquisitive about one not so quiet

indicators.note: about means the comparative for prying goes around the numeral

parts.note: nosier means more inquisitive or prying
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A busybody is asking more questions about someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Something louder is less quiet, the comparative of noisy.

clue.text: Sent girl out for hair styling

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of sent girl are thrown out of their order

explanation.surface: A girl was sent away to get her hair done.
explanation.definitionFit: Long spiral curls of hair are a classic style worn by girls.

clue.text: Checked fit (of clothes) and changed into red

indicators.note: changed signals that the letters of into red are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tried a garment for size and then changed into a red outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changed into red' reads as getting dressed in red, which suits the clothes theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting on a garment to see whether it fits is the phrasal verb used here.

clue.text: Almost deprived of snooze in Italian city

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: napless means without a nap, so deprived of a snooze

explanation.surface: A traveller in an Italian city barely got any sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoli, the capital of Campania, is known in English by this name.

clue.text: Augustus the Architect has dog at home

parts.note: a pug is a small breed of dog
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: A famous architect keeps a pet dog in his house.
explanation.definitionFit: Augustus Welby Pugin was the Victorian Gothic Revival designer behind the Houses of Parliament interiors.

clue.text: An alternative name, not as Caliph

indicators.note: not means the word as is removed from the alternative name

parts.note: an alias is an alternative name

explanation.surface: Someone says a different name won't do for a Muslim ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Ali ibn Abi Talib, cousin of Muhammad, was the fourth caliph of Islam.

clue.text: Junk guides picked up

indicators.note: in a down answer, picked up means the word for guides is lifted to read bottom to top

parts.note: maps are guides to finding your way

explanation.surface: Someone collects worthless leaflets or guidebooks.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsolicited bulk email is called this, junk mail of the internet.

clue.text: Just nothing left in New York

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation for left is placed within the city's initials

explanation.surface: Absolutely nothing remains in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Just and this word are adverbs meaning merely or no more than.

clue.text: Official permission to write verse? That stretches the truth

definitions.meaning: first meaning: read literally, a licence to be poetic
second meaning: the freedom writers take to depart from fact or rules

explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads the phrase literally as a permit for poets; the second gives its real idiomatic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the liberty an artist takes to bend facts or grammar for effect.

clue.text: Fellow gets on and copes

parts.note: a fellow is a man
to get on in years is to age, so gets on means ages

explanation.surface: A man grows older and handles it well.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who gets by or handles a difficulty successfully is said to do this.

clue.text: Slob finally agreed extra runs

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of Slob

parts.note: yes is the word of agreement

explanation.surface: A lazy cricketer at last concedes extra runs.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, byes are runs scored when the ball passes the batter and wicketkeeper without being hit.
explanation.definitionFit: These are cricket extras, runs credited to the team rather than to any batter.
